blocks.text: Dork ducked back into the driver’s compartment.
His hand went toward the firing control.
Seth got both hands under the crooked turret’s rim.
“Jenny. Clear.”
She stepped away from the tracks.
Dork’s fingers closed over the control.
Seth pulled.
Bolts cracked around the turret ring. Steel shrieked.
The whole assembly came up in his hands.
blocks.alt: Zerdo tears the complete turret from the tank, its copper-ringed ray still mounted inside and its firing cable disconnected; Dork remains in the lower hull’s driver opening.

blocks.text: A black cable stretched beneath it, pulled out of its socket and dangled loose. Dork jabbed the control. The copper opening stayed dark.
Dork looked up through the empty ring.
Seth shifted the weight away from the driver’s opening. His boots ground against the pavement.
“Your gun’s come loose,” he said.
Above the rooftops, Fist heard the tearing metal.
He glanced down.
Jaws lunged.
Fist rolled hard. Iron teeth clapped shut behind the white panel on his cuff.
“Keep looking away,” Jaws said.
Fist swung around to face him.
“Keep missing.”
Below, Dork grabbed a driving lever.
Jenny reached the driver’s opening before he could pull it.
Her white glove closed around his wrist.
“Out.”
He snatched his other hand toward the controls. She caught that one too.
Seth held the turret well to the side while Jenny hauled Dork through the lower hatch and onto the street.
blocks.alt: Jenny brings Dork out through the tank’s lower forward driver hatch to waiting officers and Billy while Zerdo holds the detached turret safely to one side.

blocks.text: His shoes scraped the armor.
“Do you know what that cost?”
Jenny kept hold of him.
“You stole it.”
Dork twisted toward the tank.
Jenny turned him back.
Billy waved two officers around the stone planter.
“This way. Keep behind the planter when you take him out.”
An officer fastened cuffs behind Dork’s back. The other took his arm.
Dork craned his neck toward the turret.
“Put that down!”
Seth bent his knees.
“I was going to.”
He lowered the assembly onto clear pavement, copper opening pointed away from the officers.
Jenny crouched beside its open underside.
Through the torn underside she could see the gray box. Two steel straps held it against the front plate. The broken control cable hung loose beneath it.
A firefighter brought a socket wrench from his truck. Jenny fitted it over the first exposed nut.
“Hold this steady.”
“I am.”
“I meant the strap.”
Seth shifted one hand.
She loosened both straps, unplugged the remaining short lead and slid the box backward. The copper rings came through the front plate with it.
blocks.alt: Jenny uses a socket wrench to release the ray’s mounting straps inside the detached turret as Zerdo steadies it; the intact gray box and copper emitter come out together.

blocks.text: One empty round opening remained.
Jaws saw the police car below.
Laura was still beside its open rear door.
He broke away from Fist and dived.
“Laura!”
Her escort looked up. The officer with the extinguisher moved with him, keeping Laura behind the open door.
Jaws opened his teeth.
Laura stepped back.
“Don’t hit the car!”
Fist cut across the dive.
His knuckles struck the side of the iron jaw.
Jaws flew sideways into the cleared square, well away from the car. He caught himself above the pavement and whirled back.
Fist stayed between him and the officers.
“You’ll have to get past me.”
Laura stared after them, furious. She stayed with her escort.
Jenny put the ray into Billy’s waiting hands.
“Keep it pointed down. Don’t touch the controls.”
Billy carried it behind the planter. An officer stayed beside him.
Jenny switched off the engine, pulled out the ignition key and checked the driver’s compartment. Empty.
She moved one of the ray’s heavy mounting straps to the curb, out of Seth’s way.
Then she looked along the street. Dork and the officers were clear. So were Laura and her escort.
She raised her hand to Seth.
“All yours.”
Seth took hold of the turret again.
This time there was no copper barrel in its front. No machine inside it. Just steel.
He lifted it high.
Behind the planter, Dork stopped struggling.
“No! That’s an Army tank!”
Seth looked at the empty hull.
“I know.”
He brought the turret down.
blocks.alt: Zerdo brings the empty turret shell down onto the evacuated tank, crushing its armor and buckling its tracks; Terminal Tower stands intact beyond the cleared street.

blocks.text: The crash rolled between the buildings.
The hull folded beneath the blow. A track snapped loose and spilled across the pavement. The other buckled under the tank’s weight.
Dust burst around Seth’s boots.
He let the turret settle into the crushed armor and stepped back.
The loose track rattled once.
Then it stopped.
Jaws turned at the crash.
He saw Dork behind the planter. The empty circle where the turret had been. The heap of steel below it.
His eyes went back to Fist.
He charged with his teeth wide open.
Fist held his place.
Closer.
The red cuff twitched.
Jaws snapped at it.
Fist dropped beneath the bite and drove upward.
His knuckles caught the iron jaw.
Jaws hit the clear pavement beside the wreck and skidded to a stop.
For a moment, his eyes would not quite focus.
Fist hovered above him, cuff safely out of reach.
Seth caught the closed metal casing between his gloves and lifted Jaws low over the empty armor, fingers clear of the teeth.
“Jenny. That bent strap.”
Jenny fetched the ray’s heavy mounting strap from the curb.
Seth bent the steel around the outside of the iron jaw. He folded its ends together beneath the casing, holding the upper and lower metal sections closed. Nothing covered Jaws’s nose or eyes.
blocks.alt: With Fist hovering beside him, Zerdo folds a heavy steel mounting strap around Jaws’s closed metal jaw casing; the bodyless head’s nose and eyes remain clear.

blocks.text: Jaws tried to bite. His teeth could not part far enough to catch the strap.
He flew toward the street. Seth caught the brace and brought him back.
“Still flies,” Fist said.
“Then I’m not letting go.”
Fist hovered beside the captive head. The red leather around his own cuff was whole.
“That’s enough biting.”
Jaws glared at him. There was still no recognition in his eyes.
An officer called for equipment to move him under guard.
Across the street, Laura watched Jenny return to her escort.
“Still want me on your team?”
Jenny glanced at the wreck, then back at her.
“If you want to help.”
Laura looked away. She gave no answer.
blocks.alt: The soaked, coatless Laura looks down beside the police car after Jenny leaves the offer to help open; officers and a firefighter maintain supervision.

blocks.text: The officer with the extinguisher stayed nearby. A fire crew brought a charged hose around the corner. Jenny warned the escort that Laura could still fire without using her hands. His partner radioed for supervised transport and a fire crew to accompany it. Nobody hurried her into an unguarded car.
Behind the planter, Billy set the ray down carefully beside the officer. Dork sat between his guards, glaring at the tank.
Fist watched Jaws. Seth held the brace.
Above them, every window of Terminal Tower caught the afternoon light.
Seth looked up.
Still there.
